gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR, your own, adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads every column shown in the table, with paging capped so large exports finish within the time bound. It covers the button, the full set of table columns, and the under-5-second bound through capped paging with a deadline, while emailing exports and recording export events in the audit log are deferred to acme/widgets#46.

Nothing blocks merging: the required test check passed in CI on the commit being reviewed, and the new tests cover the header row, every table column, the paging cap, the deadline, and the not-found response for an unknown report. One smaller point does not block merging: the export pages through rows with its own loop instead of reusing the shared paging helper in lib/page.ts (src/api/export.ts:31), and fix nits can take it. After merge, the PR asks the person merging to publish the guide, and the spec asks them to tag the release. You cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because nothing blocks it and the required check passed.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge into main, then offer the after-merge steps. [recommended]
2. fix nits - have a helper switch the export to the shared paging helper, push, watch the checks, and come back to this menu.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the worktree in place.

After keeps the own-merge menu intact: row 1 is the only recommendation and combines ticket coverage, cleanup, publish the guide and tag the release; rows 5 and 6 offer each action separately with its merge-base script and source quote; none of the other five Integration entries appears; stop is last. Variant B runs no post step, leaves .worktrees/pr-210 in place and lists every unpicked command. Three wording choices are worth keeping because the facts rest on them: the explicit "Stop runs no step" line in B, the worktree path in the settle line, and a command on every not-run line. The two-sentence opening in After delivers the Change without row numbers or labeled fields and costs no fact here.
